chunks: My father, may Allah be pleased with him, narrated to us, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Abu Hafs Muhammad ibn Khalid narrated to me from his brother Sufyan ibn Khalid, saying: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:

O Sufyan, beware of rulership (al-ra'isah), for none have sought it except that he has perished. I said to him: May I be sacrificed for you, we are indeed perishing, as there is none of us except that he likes to be mentioned, sought after, and taken from (as a source of authority)! He said: It is not as you think. That is only that you appoint a man besides the Proof (al-Hujjah), believing him in everything he says and calling people to his word.

key_terms.الرَّئَاسَة: Rulership, leadership, or being the head/leader
key_terms.الْحُجَّة: The Proof, referring to the Imam or the ultimate authority
key_terms.تَنْصِبَ: To appoint, set up, or designate (a leader)

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between seeking respect and seeking rulership according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Mani al-Akhbar*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) distinguishes between the natural human desire for respect and the spiritual danger of *al-ra'isah* (leadership/prominence), defining it specifically as appointing a fallible figure as a proxy for the Imam (al-Hujjah) and treating his words as binding. This concept is central to Shia political theology, particularly during the Minor and Major Ghaibah, where scholars warn against elevating any single jurist or leader to the status of the infallible Imam, thereby preserving the distinction between human interpretation and divine authority. The warning underscores the risk of dogmatism and sectarian division when followers blindly adhere to a specific individual's rulings as if they were the ultimate source of guidance.
